name: PingUp.ai – AI Chatbot & AI Agent
author: etinet

sections.description:
PingUp.ai connects your WordPress site to your PingUp account and adds your AI chat assistant to the site frontend.

  • One-click, secure connection to your PingUp account (OAuth-style authorization with PKCE — no passwords or API keys to copy around).
  • Pick which of your PingUp bots to show on the site.
  • Enable or disable the widget with a single toggle.
  • Disconnect at any time; the connection can also be revoked from the PingUp dashboard.

The plugin does nothing until you connect it. Before you click “Connect to PingUp” on the settings page, the plugin sends no data anywhere, loads no remote code and contacts no external service.

External services

This plugin relies on PingUp, a third-party hosted AI chat assistant service, to work.

Once you have connected your account, selected a bot and enabled the widget:

  • Your site’s frontend loads the PingUp widget script from PingUp’s servers and displays the chat widget to your visitors.
  • Messages that visitors type into the chat widget are sent to and processed by the PingUp service in order to generate replies.
  • Your WordPress server communicates with the PingUp API (to list your bots, to manage the connection and to verify twice a day that the connection has not been revoked) using a revocable, site-specific access token stored in your WordPress options.

No data is sent to PingUp before you explicitly connect the plugin to your PingUp account, and nothing is loaded on your site’s frontend until you also select a bot.

Service provider: PingUp — Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the pingupai folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings → PingUp.ai and click “Connect to PingUp”.
  4. Log in to PingUp (if needed) and authorize this site.
  5. Back in WordPress, pick the bot you want to show and save.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin contact PingUp before I connect it?

No. The plugin is completely inert until you click “Connect to PingUp” on the settings page. It performs no requests to PingUp (or anyone else), loads no remote code and sends no data before that.

Do I need a PingUp account?

Yes. The plugin only displays bots that you have created in your PingUp account. Without an account (and without connecting it) the plugin does nothing.

What data is shared with PingUp?

When you connect, PingUp learns your site URL and site name. After you enable the widget, messages your visitors type into the chat are processed by the PingUp service to generate replies. See PingUp’s Privacy Policy for details.

How do I remove the widget from my site?

Untick “Show the chat widget on this site” on the settings page, or disconnect the site entirely. Deactivating the plugin also removes the widget, and uninstalling deletes everything the plugin stored.

Where is the access token stored, and can I revoke it?

The site-specific access token is stored in your WordPress options table (readable by site administrators only). You can revoke it at any time by disconnecting from the settings page, or remotely from the PingUp dashboard. After a remote revocation the plugin detects the invalid connection during its twice-daily connection check (or immediately, the next time an administrator opens the plugin settings) and then shows a reconnect notice and stops injecting the widget.
sections.changelog:
0.1.1

  • Admin brand styles moved from an inline style block to an enqueued stylesheet (assets/admin.css), loaded only on the plugin page.
  • Removed bundled translation files and the load_plugin_textdomain() call: translations are delivered by translate.wordpress.org.

0.1.0

  • Initial release: secure connect flow (authorization code + PKCE), bot selection with cached list, enable/disable toggle, frontend widget injection, disconnect.
